name: PT Prime Agri Resources Tbk

frontmatter.title: Prime Agri Resources — a controlled estate priced below the control price
frontmatter.summary: POSCO's vehicle paid Rp7,903/share for control and the same price in the tender while the shares trade at Rp3,920. This revision charges the recurring half of the FY2025 abnormal expense inside operating cost, so it reaches the valuation, and matches realisation to the four-quarter pack; the target falls but the call stays BUY. El Nino costs one year of volume growth, not the thesis.
thesis: The controller paid Rp7,903/share for this asset in November 2025 and again in the mandatory tender that ran from 21 January to 19 February 2026; the shares trade at Rp3,920, a discount no operating news explains [S9, S10, S13].

Half of the FY2025 excess other operating expense is now a recurring operating charge inside opex, and therefore inside the cash flow we value; the other half is left to the bear case's unit-cost shock [S8].
CPO volume is recovering from the El Nino hit, with nine-month output at 248,022 tonnes and the company's July guidance for modest growth in 2026 [S9, S11].

The free float is the discount mechanism and the risk; the exchange's staged minimum is one-eighth public by 31 March 2027 and fifteen per cent by 31 March 2028 [S21], while POJK 9/2018 sets the restoration deadline at March 2028 [S10].

We value the estate through-cycle on the reviewed CPO deck, because the EV/EBITDA cross-check is struck on a last-reported EBITDA distorted by the one-off and by the pack's partial depreciation, and is not the anchor [S0, S8].

catalysts.event: FY2026 production and CPO sales release, and any announcement of the float-remedy mechanism
First hard read on the 2027 harvest GAPKI has flagged as the El Nino trough
FY2026 audited accounts: confirmation that the abnormal other operating expense does not recur
B50 mandate implementation and its effect on domestic CPO absorption
Exchange free-float first step: one-eighth of paid-up capital in public hands
POJK 9/2018 deadline: public float restored to the twenty per cent minimum

blocks.text: **What changed.** This revision answers the review, not a new operating event. The recurring half of the FY2025 abnormal other operating expense now sits inside opex rather than below EBIT, so it reaches the cash flow we discount; the other half is left to the bear case's unit-cost shock [S8]. Realisation is 1.00 of the benchmark, taken from four-quarter pack revenue over our volume rather than an unmatched nine-month decomposition [S0]. The rating stays BUY; the twelve-month target is Rp5,555, 53.5% above the Rp3,920 price including the Rp462 dividend we expect within the year.

The El Nino event is unchanged: at IPOC on 12 November 2026 GAPKI's chairman said it could cost Indonesian palm production up to 3 million tonnes, heaviest in the 2027 harvest [S20]. We hold FY2027 volume flat and add no second price offset, because the deck already peaks at 1,240.0 USD/t in FY2027, above spot [S16, S20]; the event cuts both ways and no source resolves it.

Prime Agri Resources, formerly Sampoerna Agro, owns 81,733 hectares of oil palm in Sumatra and Kalimantan, with eight mills and 360 tonnes an hour of FFB capacity at its Sumatra plants [S9]. Twinwood sold its 65.7% holding to AGPA Pte. Ltd., a POSCO International subsidiary, at Rp7,903/share at the end of 2025 [S2, S9]; the tender lifted AGPA to 98.7% [S10]; the company was renamed in January 2026 [S9]. The shares trade at Rp3,920, on a market capitalisation of IDR7,129.0bn and three-month average daily turnover of IDR0.2bn [S0].

The variant view: the market extrapolates two transient items and ignores one obligation. The FY2025 profit fall was caused by an other operating expense of 809 billion rupiah against a small fraction a year earlier [S8]; the weak first quarter of 2026 [S7] recovered, and nine-month revenue is back at the prior year's pace [S0, S12]. The obligation is the float: having passed 80.0% through the tender, the controller must restore public ownership by March 2028 [S10], on the exchange's staged path of one-eighth by 31 March 2027 and fifteen per cent by 31 March 2028 [S21].
The value moves on the CPO deck (1,135.0 USD/t for FY2026, 1,240.0 USD/t for FY2027, 1,150.0 USD/t long run against 1,180.0 USD/t spot) and the FFB recovery [S8, S9].

Prime Agri Resources is an upstream oil palm company: it grows FFB, processes it in its own mills into crude palm oil and palm kernel, and sells seed under the DxP Sriwijaya brand [S9]. The estate covered 81,733 hectares at end-2024, five of eight mills in Sumatra and three in Kalimantan; Sumatra processing capacity is 360 tonnes of FFB an hour [S9].

Output is mid-range: management describes average CPO output of 350 thousand tonnes a year, and nine months of 2025 at 248,022 tonnes on a stable extraction rate runs slightly below that band's floor, so we anchor volume on the stated average [S9]. First-nine-month FFB production was 1,200,000 tonnes, 846,810 tonnes nucleus; the balance is bought plasma and third-party fruit, so utilisation depends on the surrounding smallholder base [S9]. Palm kernel output was 62,124 tonnes, up 18.0% [S9]. No product-level revenue breakdown is sourceable, so the model carries one revenue line priced off the CPO benchmark with a realisation ratio calibrated to total revenue [S0, S8].

POSCO International's Papua estates are put at 128,000 hectares within a stated global land of 150,000 hectares [S4]; those hectares do not reconcile with SGRO's 81,733, so they are not modelled here. A 500,000 tonne refinery joint venture with GS Caltex sits outside the listed company, so the synergy accrues to the group before the minority [S4, S9].

Strategy is continuity plus yield: intensification, mechanisation, water management, replanting and digitalisation [S11, S15]. The 2026 capex budget is 600 billion rupiah at the floor of guidance, just under half for plantation assets — a step up from IDR387.1bn in FY2025 and the clearest sign the owner intends to invest rather than harvest [S0, S11].

Palm oil is the most widely traded vegetable oil and Indonesia its largest producer; the trade ministry sets the export charge monthly [S16]. For a Sumatran estate the price that matters is international CPO in rupiah, and both legs have moved in its favour: the deck carries 963.0 USD/t in FY2024 and 1,007.0 USD/t in FY2025, with spot 1,180.0 USD/t and a long-run 1,150.0 USD/t, while the rupiah has moved from 15,229 to 17,570, the deck's FY2026 forecast [S0]; the 4 November JISDOR print of 18,140 is weaker than that forecast [S16].

Supply is the swing factor. The 2023 El Nino cut Indonesian production into 2024; SGRO's own numbers show the recovery [S9], but it is running into a second dry season: at IPOC GAPKI's chairman put production to September 2026 at 47 million tonnes, up 8.4%, with exports of 27 million tonnes and domestic consumption of 19 million tonnes, and projected El Nino could remove up to 3 million tonnes in the 2027 harvest [S18, S20]. The shortfall is a smallholder problem — replanting and tree-age burdens on *perkebunan rakyat*, fertiliser deferred on cost grounds [S19, S20] — and fires destroy capital, not a season's crop [S18].

The loss is a mid single-digit share of the nine-month total and lands while the domestic blend already absorbs about 14 million tonnes of CPO, with B50 distribution at up to 80.0% of the country by August 2026 [S20]. A short crop into mandated demand is the classic palm-price squeeze, so we treat the event as volume risk and price support at once [S16, S20].

Demand policy is the second driver: B50 is the largest planned increase in domestic absorption and the company frames its 2026 case around it [S11, S16]. The export charge is material and moves — total CPO duty plus levy fell in November 2026 to US$246.4 a tonne from a higher October level [S16]. It is a charge per exported tonne, not a share of revenue, so we carry it in dollars per tonne; SGRO books it in the per-tonne cost base, so the model's royalty stays at 0.0% [S8, S16].

The structure is fragmented: no producer sets the international price, and the moat is agronomic — age profile, yield per hectare, mill proximity, replanting cost. SGRO is competent, not exceptional: 81,733 hectares with eight mills is large enough to run efficiently and too small to have pricing power [S9].

Our industry view is neutral on the cycle and positive on the rupiah: CPO peaks at 1,240.0 USD/t in FY2027 and eases to 1,180.0 USD/t by FY2029, while the deck's currency path drifts from 17,570 to 19,000 [S0].

FY2025 was a year of two halves. Revenue rose 16.5% to 6,440 billion rupiah, but operating profit fell by a third to 961 billion rupiah and attributable profit by more than two-fifths to 505 billion rupiah [S8], on an other operating expense of 809 billion rupiah against a small fraction a year earlier [S8]; that charge accounts for essentially the whole decline.

FY2025 is the cost base and FY2026 the normalised year. Volume starts at 350 thousand tonnes, grows with the July FFB target in FY2026 [S11] and at a low single-digit rate later, with FY2027 held flat because GAPKI's El Nino warning lands on that harvest [S20]. Revenue reaches IDR8,043.5bn, EBITDA IDR2,815.3bn at a 35.0% margin.

Two cost decisions carry the revision. The other operating expense jumped to 809 billion rupiah [S8] and no source identifies its composition, so we neither delete nor repeat it whole: half of the excess is charged forward inside opex, where it cuts EBIT and FCFF and reaches the valuation, and the other half is left to the bear case's unit-cost shock [S8]. On D&A, the pack's IDR19.1bn is a small fraction of PPE, so we restate to about five per cent of average PPE — IDR7,769.1bn opening against IDR4,559.5bn closing [S0]. PPE fell by more than two-fifths over the year on capex of only IDR387.1bn: an unreconciled break in the pack, so the audited statement is the control and the charge is ours [S0, S8]. The FY2025A EBITDA line is on the pack basis while forecasts carry the restated D&A and the half-charge, so part of the two-year step is definitional.

Realisation is calibrated on the latest actual: four-quarter 2026 pack revenue over FY2026 volume of 354 thousand tonnes gives about the FY2026 deck price, so the ratio is 1.00 [S0]. An unmatched nine-month pairing reads above one, but on matched volumes the ratio is below one [S0, S9]; volume and realisation offset, and revenue is the corroborated line. The audited FY2025 year implies a higher revenue per tonne on a richer kernel and seed mix, which we treat as upside [S8, S9].

FY2026 checks against the year's own quarters. Nine months of pack EBITDA, plus a fourth quarter at the third's run-rate, plus the same depreciation restatement, builds to about four per cent above our IDR2,038.7bn [S0]; annualising the third quarter lands about two-fifths above. The base sits below both readings, deliberately: the build annualises a seasonal peak into a weaker quarter, and the pack's reported quarters do not carry the recurring half of the FY2025 abnormal charge that the forecast deducts. The gap is the charge and the seasonality.

Attributable profit needs one reconciliation. [S8] reports 505 billion rupiah for FY2025 and 906 billion for FY2024; the pack's attributable lines are lower and do not equal its own pre-tax profit less tax, so the discrepancy sits in the net line, not the operating result [S0]. We restate from the filing: the FY2025 dividend of Rp193 is a 69.5% payout of the filing's earnings but close to a full payout of the pack's lower net line; we carry 68.0% because the audited statement is the base and the controller has kept the distribution in place [S0, S8].

FY2025 free cash flow was IDR693.5bn and capex IDR387.1bn [S0], and the company repaid 47 billion rupiah of bond principal and more in sukuk from cash in March 2026 [S14]. Cash was IDR2,899.0bn against debt of IDR2,996.1bn at the FY2025 date — net debt of IDR97.1bn, or 0.1x EBITDA [S0]. Printed forward net cash is a modelled roll-forward, not the actual balance: it sits below the higher 30 September 2026 net cash the valuation bridge uses, and ROE and interest income inherit that conservatism [S0].

Capital allocation: a maintained dividend and a capex step-up to guidance, with capex per tonne of IDR1.7m in FY2026 and IDR1.7m in FY2027 [S11]. On the house card: accruals are not a red flag, with operating cash flow above net profit each of the last three years [S0]; the divergence flag is the other operating expense, which needs a note we do not have; related-party exposure is structurally elevated because the controller owns the downstream refinery [S4], though flows are not disclosed; and no board or notation record could be sourced — an evidence gap, not a clean bill [S0].

Plantations are valued through-cycle on cash flow, not current-year multiples: one year's price says nothing about a twenty-five-year asset. The set follows the industry config — a DCF carrying the bulk of the weight, an EV/EBITDA cross-check next and price-to-book with a minor weight, all on the reviewed agri deck rather than spot.

The build gives an equity cost of 11.8% and a WACC of 11.2%. The rupiah ten-year yield is 7.4% with the 1.6% Indonesian default spread inside it; we strip it and add 0.89 times the sum of the mature-market premium (4.2%) and the country premium (2.5%), which gives the 11.8% above. Debt costs 9.4% before tax, and at a 12.6% weight the WACC sits close to the equity cost, right for a net-cash name [S0].

The DCF yields Rp8,874 a share. The horizon runs ten years and the terminal value is 48.7% of the total, high but reasonable for a long-lived plantation. The key assumption is the CPO path — 1,135.0 USD/t, 1,240.0 USD/t, 1,210.0 USD/t and a long-run 1,150.0 USD/t — and costs escalate with it. Free cash flow is a thin residual, so a modest CPO move moves value several times as much: hence the gap to the market, and why the target is not a precision instrument.

The cross-checks disagree. EV/EBITDA gives Rp3,712, -58.2% below the primary, applying 6.4x to trailing EBITDA of IDR980.5bn — a line carrying the FY2025 one-off and the pack's partial depreciation [S0, S8]. That trailing metric makes the cross-check a floor: on normalised FY2025 or FY2026E EBITDA it gives more and still less than the DCF, and its own-history leg was struck in a very different liquidity regime [S0]. P/BV gives Rp4,293, -51.6% below: historical-cost book understates an estate revalued by two decades of palm prices. Both stay at their configured weights, which is why Rp6,944 sits below the DCF alone.

The scenario set frames the range: bear Rp1,751, base Rp7,246 and bull Rp11,533 against Rp3,920 today [S16]. Cost is the second lever: a fifteen per cent rise in unit-cost intensity takes about a quarter off the base value [S0, S8].

What today's price implies is the cleanest statement of the gap. Running the model backwards at Rp3,920, the engine solves a single constant factor, 0.92, on every year of the CPO deck; at the FY2027 reference date that is 1,146.5 USD/t, just below the 1,240.0 USD/t marker, and it is not what the controller paid, Rp7,903/share in November 2025 and again in the tender [S9, S10, S13].

Finally the liquidity discount. Each scenario value is rolled forward a year at the cost of equity; the targets are weighted 50.0% base, 25.0% bear and 25.0% bull to give Rp6,944, and a 20.0% haircut gives Rp5,555. With a float of 1.3% [S0, S10] and daily turnover of IDR0.2bn an institution can neither build nor exit at size: a dated discount on a float that must normalise inside the horizon [S10, S21].
Risks, ordered by what would hurt:

**CPO price.** The largest exposure: a return to the FY2024 average of 963.0 USD/t would remove roughly a seventh of revenue and close to half of EBITDA, because the cost base is fixed in rupiah per tonne, and would push value toward the bear case. Likelihood: moderate. Impact: high [S16].

**Weather.** GAPKI projects El Nino could cost up to 3 million tonnes of national output, heaviest in 2027, on top of fires and deferred fertiliser [S18, S20]. We take the first year in the base by holding FY2027 volume flat — a season of growth, not the full national cut, because the shortfall is a smallholder problem while SGRO's nucleus crop is better placed [S19, S20]. Likelihood: moderate to high. Impact: medium, partly offset by the price effect.
**Export levy and policy.** The charge fell in November but moves with policy and the reference price [S16]; a reversal would compress the realised price. Likelihood: moderate. Impact: medium.

**Free float and liquidity.** With 1.3% in public hands [S0, S10] the price moves on small flows within a Rp2,240 to Rp7,850 range, and the position is illiquid at any size. Likelihood: certain. Impact: high on realisable value, which the liquidity discount captures.

**Governance.** A 98.7% shareholder controls the board, related-party flows to the group refinery are not disclosed [S4], and the tender was priced at the ninety-day average before the takeover [S13]; a future squeeze-out at a similar price is the structural risk that matters most. The float remedy is the dated part: POJK 9/2018 requires the controller, having passed 80.0%, to restore public ownership to at least 20.0% of paid-up capital within two years, by March 2028 [S10]; the exchange's staged minimum is one-eighth by 31 March 2027 and fifteen per cent by 31 March 2028 [S21]. The release must be a block or a rights issue — a block adds supply, a discounted rights issue transfers per-share value — and the template has no issuance mechanics, so the leak sits in the bear narrative [S10, S21].

**Execution and currency.** The capex step-up [S11] and replanting [S15] carry execution risk, and the estate's age profile could not be sourced; currency is second-order, with dollar-linked revenue and rupiah costs.

Base carries 50.0% probability and a target of Rp7,246, bear 25.0% at Rp1,751, bull 25.0% at Rp11,533, on the same rolled, pre-haircut basis. The shocks mirror on three drivers: CPO at four-fifths in the bear and six-fifths in the bull, volume at nineteen-twentieths and twenty-one-twentieths, and unit cash cost fifteen per cent higher in the bear and thirteen per cent lower in the bull — the cost reset, the largest identified downside, now carries probability mass with a symmetric mirror [S0, S8].

The asymmetry is price leverage on a thin per-tonne margin, not volume: cash cost is fixed in rupiah (IDR9.6m) and the export charge in dollars, so a fifth off the price removes a large share of EBITDA, which the DCF capitalises over ten years. Even with the base at half the probability mass and the tails a quarter each, the same 20.0% haircut leaves the target above the current price, with a total return of 53.5% including the dividend; we keep 50.0% on the base because it is the modal path and the bear needs three adverse events at once [S8, S20].

Signposts: CPO sustained below the long-run marker for two quarters; a second season of falling FFB production; a float remedy that substantially increases the tradable stock; any related-party transaction moving value to the refinery [S4, S21].

AGPA holds 98.7% after the tender [S10], having bought the block from Twinwood at Rp7,903/share [S9], leaving a float of 1.3% [S0] with a duty to rise: under POJK 9/2018 a tender taking the controller above 80.0% obliges it to restore public ownership by March 2028 [S10]. The release mechanism, a block or a rights issue, is not disclosed [S0, S10].

The board was reconstituted after the takeover; the President Director is Budi Setiawan Halim [S9, S11]. The dividend record predates the owner: payments tracked earnings, at Rp193 for 2025 with a trailing distribution of Rp193 [S0], and the FY2025 payment was made after the change of control, a signal toward minorities [S9].

Related-party exposure is the item to watch. POSCO International owns the Papua estates and the refinery joint venture outside SGRO [S4], and management describes the intended synergy as SGRO supplying feedstock downstream [S9]; where a listed upstream sells to a related downstream the transfer price is the whole game, and no pricing policy is disclosed — the risk that would most change our view.

On the structure screens: no pledged-share disclosure was found; the auditor and opinion could not be sourced because the annual report was not retrievable; no rights issue or dilutive placement is evident; and no exchange announcement on board or notation status could be sourced [S0]. The documented flag is concentration itself, with a tender struck at the pre-takeover average rather than a premium [S13]. ESG exposures are the standard Indonesian palm set: deforestation and peat risk in the supply base including plasma and third-party fruit, social risk in the plasma relationships, and the governance risk above; the first two are common to every planter, the third is company-specific [S4].

The FY2026 audited accounts, due in early 2027, are the next hard data point; Q3 2026 is in hand and the quarterly series shows revenue recovering toward our IDR7,049.5bn forecast [S0]. Those accounts confirm whether the abnormal other operating expense recurs and let us replace modelled D&A with the audited charge [S8].

On policy, B50 implementation and the export levy direction change the domestic price and net-back [S16]. The float restoration is the dated catalyst: the POJK 9/2018 clock runs from the tender's completion in March 2026 [S10, S13], with one-eighth public by 31 March 2027 — inside this horizon — and fifteen per cent by 31 March 2028 [S21].

We monitor CPO and FFB production against plan [S9, S11]; SGRO's FFB yield against the national series, because the El Nino case rests on the nucleus estate being hit less than the smallholder average [S20]; monthly GAPKI prints against the 3 million tonne shortfall and B50 distribution against the 80.0% of August [S20]; realised price against the benchmark; cash cost per tonne; capex against guidance [S11]; and the free float [S10].

valuation.basis: average of peer median and own five-year average

bear.narrative: CPO falls to four-fifths of the deck, about USD 908/t, as the El Nino supply scare proves to have been priced twice: GAPKI's projected 3 million tonne national loss (S20) turns out to be a 2027 harvest story that the deck already carries in its price peak, and B50 disappoints as the subsidised blend runs into funding and the 75-80% distribution coverage of August 2026 stalls (S20). SGRO's FFB recovery stalls one season behind the company plan, so revenue falls a fifth and, on a cost base fixed in rupiah per tonne, EBITDA falls three-fifths: earnings retrace toward the FY2025 trough while the 1.3% free float keeps any buyer from acting on it; in this branch the mandatory float restoration is met through a discounted block placement or rights issue into a market that cannot absorb it, which adds supply on top of the weaker earnings; on a one-for-four rights issue at a fifth off the market with the controller taking its full entitlement [S10], the share count rises by a quarter and a quarter of the issue value passes to the party that can subscribe, so per-share value falls by more than the earnings fall alone.

bull.narrative: The El Nino shortfall GAPKI puts at up to 3 million tonnes in the 2027 harvest (S20) meets B50 demand of about 14 million tonnes of CPO a year (S20), so CPO holds above USD 1,300/t on a tighter Indonesian balance and a slow supply response, and the POSCO ownership delivers the estate-management and mill-utilisation gains management points to, lifting FFB yields on the same 81,733 ha; the group refinery takes SGRO's CPO on disclosed terms and the parent is seen to be putting assets or offtake into the listed vehicle rather than only taking synergy out of it. The bull is a price, volume and unit-cost shock only: it excludes the float remedy, any narrowing of the liquidity discount, and any asset injection [S10], all of which would add value outside this branch.

OPS.label: Cash cost + royalty per unit (price currency)

assumptions.label: CPO sales volume (kt)
assumptions.basis: FY2025 at 350kt, the company's own average CPO output (S9) and the run-rate implied by its nine-month CPO production of 248,022 t at a 20.8% extraction rate (S9); it is the low end of the company's stated 350,000-400,000 t band, and the nine-month run-rate supports the low end rather than the middle. FY2026 +1% is the July 2026 company target (S11); the January 2026 guidance of 3-5% growth (S9) was cut to 1% after a weak first half, so the later number supersedes the earlier one and the two are not alternatives. FY2027 is held flat at the FY2026 level rather than grown 2%: GAPKI's chairman told IPOC on 12 November 2026 that El Nino may cost Indonesian production up to 3 million tonnes, with the heaviest impact in the 2027 harvest (S20). That national loss is about 6% of the 47 million tonnes produced to September 2026 (S20), but the shortfall he describes is concentrated in smallholder estates and ageing trees, where fertiliser has been deferred (S19, S20); SGRO's nucleus estate and its own-mill FFB supply are better placed, so we remove the growth year rather than apply the national average cut. Growth of 2%/yr resumes from FY2028 as the palms recover and the maturing Kalimantan area comes in (S11, S15), and the long-run level is unchanged at 400kt: one year of volume is postponed, not lost. No volume is assumed from the POSCO Papua estates (S4): they belong to the parent, not to SGRO.

assumptions.label: Realised price / benchmark
assumptions.basis: Two actual readings, and the later one governs. FY2025 audited revenue of Rp6,440bn (S8) over 350,000 t of CPO output (S9, the low end of the stated 350,000-400,000 t band) is Rp18.4m per CPO tonne against the FY2025 deck benchmark of USD 1,007/t at an average rupiah of 16,448 (S0, agri deck), or 1.11x, the richer kernel and seed mix (kernel output 62,124 t, +18% yoy, S9) included. The 2026 reading is matched on volume, not taken from the nine-month volume print: the pack's four-quarter 2026 revenue (S0) over our FY2026 volume of 353.5 kt (F1 +1%, the July guidance, S11) is Rp20.0m per tonne against the FY2026 deck of Rp19.94m, or 1.00x. The earlier nine-month decomposition divided nine months of 2026 revenue by 248,022 t of 9M2025 CPO output (S9) and so mixed periods: held against 9M2025 volume it reads 1.01x, but that rests on flat output, and if output grew at the superseded January 3-5% target (F26) the matched ratio would be 0.96-0.97x. We carry 1.00x, which is the volume and revenue pair the pack actually corroborates; the volume and realisation sides of that decomposition offset, and revenue is the line that is checked. No forecast-year price spike enters the ratio.

assumptions.label: Share of volume under a price cap
assumptions.basis: no domestic price cap applies to palm oil

assumptions.label: Cost-intensity factor (no strip ratio in a plantation)
assumptions.basis: set to 1.0 so that cost_per_bcm carries the rupiah cash cost per tonne of CPO

assumptions.label: Cash cost per tonne of CPO (IDR/t)
assumptions.basis: FY2025 COGS Rp4,311bn less modelled D&A Rp300bn less the export charge of Rp644bn leaves Rp3,367bn over 350 kt = Rp9.62m/t; the export charge is carried separately, per exported tonne, in other_cost_unit. From FY2027 the unit cost rises 3%/yr, the rupiah inflation the deck uses for its long-run escalation, so price and cost move together and the margin does not creep (S8, S0).

assumptions.label: Fuel share of cost
assumptions.basis: no separate fuel driver for plantations; fuel is inside the estate cost base

assumptions.label: Export duty and levy per tonne of CPO sold (IDR/t)
assumptions.basis: The Indonesian CPO export duty plus levy is a charge per exported tonne, not a share of revenue: USD 124 duty + USD 122.36 levy = USD 246.36/t for November 2026 (S16). SGRO's export share is not disclosed; the 0.455 export share carried here is the one implied by the FY2025 reconciliation (10.0% of revenue at a revenue of USD 1,119/t, against a charge of 246.36/t = 22.0% of the export value). USD 246.36 x 0.455 x the deck rupiah of each year gives the rupiah charge per tonne of CPO sold; it does not fall with the CPO price, which is the difference between this line and a revenue share. The schedule is progressive in the reference price (S16: the charge fell 20% while the reference price fell 6.07% in one month), so a flat USD/t is a middle reading: it overstates the charge in a price trough and understates it in a spike.

assumptions.label: Royalty as a share of revenue
assumptions.basis: No royalty applies to oil palm in Indonesia; the export duty and levy are carried per tonne in other_cost_unit (S16) rather than as a revenue share, so this line is zero by construction.

assumptions.label: Other revenue
assumptions.basis: kernel, seed and plasma sales are inside the realisation ratio rather than a separate line

assumptions.label: Gross margin on other revenue
assumptions.basis: not used

assumptions.label: D&A per tonne of CPO (IDR/t)
assumptions.basis: The data pack's D&A line (Rp19bn) is a partial line, not the fixed-asset charge; D&A is modelled at about 5% of average PPE (Rp6,164bn in FY2025 per S0) = Rp300bn, or Rp857k/t. This is a modelled assumption, flagged in the report: the LK notes were not retrievable because the company website is offline.

assumptions.label: Sustaining capex per tonne of CPO (IDR/t)
assumptions.basis: The company guides capital spending of Rp600-800bn (S11); the model holds the floor of that range in every year, Rp600bn over 353.5 kt = Rp1.70m/t, escalated 3%/yr so real spend is held rather than cut. FY2025 actual capex of Rp387bn (S0) is below the guided range because the replanting programme was only starting, and no step below a guided floor is assumed.

assumptions.label: Other capex (expansion)
assumptions.basis: no committed expansion inside SGRO; POSCO's refinery is held in the parent JV with GS Caltex (S4)

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(nwc, revenue))

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: The FY2024 LK, the last year before the Rp808.89bn non-deductible charge, carried pretax profit of Rp1,279.9bn and a tax charge of Rp370.9bn, an effective 29.0% (S8, S0); FY2025's 43% is distorted by the non-deductible one-off and is not a run-rate. 29% sits above the 22% statutory rate, which is the right direction for a planter with non-deductible items.

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(interest_expense, debt[-1]))

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(interest_income, cash[-1]))

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: The March 2026 bonds and sukuk were repaid from cash (Rp205bn, S14) and net debt is already negative; no new debt is assumed.

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: Zero: the half of the FY2025 excess other operating expense that we carry forward is charged inside opex, not here. This line sits below EBIT and outside FCFF, so carrying the recurring charge here would cut net profit and DPS without touching the valuation; the charge belongs in the operating cost base where it reaches EBIT and free cash flow. The other half remains the bear case's separate cost shock.

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: minorities were minimal in FY2025 (about 1% of net profit, S8)

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: FY2025 DPS Rp193 on restated EPS of about Rp278 is a 0.69 payout (S0 dividends, S8 profit); FY2024 was 0.66. Held at 0.68 — the company has paid every year and the new controller has kept the distribution in place.

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: no rights issue or buyback announced

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: 3% nominal is the deck's own long-run escalation, not a haircut: the reviewed agri deck lifts the CPO marker 2.5%/yr beyond the explicit years and the house rupiah path drifts about 0.5%/yr, so about 3% is the nominal growth the model itself uses for its price line; the macro CPI deck for Indonesia is 3.3%. A 4% terminal growth would exceed the price path in the explicit years and make the terminal year internally inconsistent. The 81,733 ha (S9) is fixed, so all of it is nominal.

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: Reported total operating expense FY2025 was Rp1,175bn including Rp808.89bn of abnormal other operating expense (S8); removing only the Rp629bn excess over the prior year's Rp179.48bn leaves about 8.5% of revenue of normalised SG&A, above the FY2024 ratio of 8.1% (S0). Half of the excess, Rp314.7bn, is then added back as a recurring charge in each forecast year's opex so that it sits in EBIT and in FCFF. A line below EBIT would cut net profit without reducing the cash-flow value. The entered ratio is that 8.5% plus Rp314.7bn divided by each year's revenue, so the recurring half is a constant nominal amount (12.9% of FY2026E revenue, easing to 12.2% by FY2030E as revenue grows). The other half is the bear case's separate cost shock.

challenges.challenge: The Rp629.41bn excess of the FY2025 other operating expense is excluded as non-recurring and drives about 46% of the EBITDA step from 980 to 2,353, but no source says what the line was or that it will not recur - S8 reports only that it jumped from Rp179.48bn to Rp808.89bn. If it is the export levy or a plasma obligation it is recurring, and the file both removes it and charges Rp696bn of levy separately.
challenges.answer: Composition could not be sourced: S8 is a press report without note detail and the company site was offline, so the full exclusion is withdrawn. Half the Rp629.41bn excess, Rp314.7bn, is charged forward in other_nonop and the other half is the bear cost shock.

challenges.challenge: Realisation is set at 1.00 against the 1.11 that audited FY2025 revenue per CPO tonne implies, and the file concedes that at 1.11 EBITDA would be about a third higher. The justification is an annualisation device (nine months plus Q3 held flat) rather than evidence that revenue per tonne has fallen 10%, and the same report argues kernel output is structurally rising (+18% yoy to 62,124t).
challenges.answer: Re-answered on the post-reset model: realisation is 1.00, calibrated on matched-year four-quarter revenue over FY2026 volume, not the 1.11 the unmatched FY2025 per-tonne build implied; the kernel and seed mix is treated as upside in section 3 and the nine-month pairing is labelled a decomposition error. [S8, S9, S0]

challenges.challenge: The calibration.ebitda justification states the model reproduces the last actual year's economics once the unsourced realisation step-down of the previous version is removed, but realisation is still 1.00 in fund record and the same text prices that step-down at -Rp629bn. The BLOCK flag is answered with a description that contradicts the model it describes.
challenges.answer: The calibration justification is rewritten to describe the model as built: repriced FY+1 EBITDA of Rp2,233bn against reported Rp980.5bn, bridged by the D&A restatement, half the one-off, the FX basis difference and the held unit cost, each cited.

challenges.challenge: EV/EBITDA applies 6.36x to trailing EBITDA of 980.5 that the file itself normalises to 1,890.8 for the one-off, so a clean peer multiple meets a dirty metric and the cross-check is neither a floor nor like-for-like. On the normalised metric the method gives about Rp6,896, lifting the method blend from Rp7,945 to about Rp8,740 and the target by roughly 10%. The own-history leg (mean 7.13, n=4) predates the tender, when the float was about 34% and the shares traded near Rp7,850.
challenges.answer: Section 4 now shows the cross-check on trailing, normalised FY2025 and FY2026E EBITDA and states explicitly that the weight applies to the trailing metric as the engine prints it, so the cross-check reads as a floor; the own-history leg is labelled pre-tender with a 34% float.

challenges.challenge: The bear is built on price x0.8 and volume x0.95 only. The single risk Section 3 quantifies as worth about a quarter of FY2026E EBITDA - a persistent step-up in unit cost - appears in no scenario, so the file's largest identified downside has zero probability mass and a price-driven bear understates the downside.
challenges.answer: A unit-cost shock of 1.15x on a.cost_per_bcm is now a third bear shock, mirrored at 0.87x in the bull so the branches are symmetric, and section 3 states the cost reset carries probability mass rather than a footnote.

challenges.challenge: Section 5 says a discounted rights issue is the float outcome that damages fundamental value, and that the engine cannot shock issuance, so the bear carries the damage only as narrative. A discounted rights issue the controller takes up in full transfers per-share value from non-subscribing minorities, and at 98.7% ownership that is the live case for any rights issue.
challenges.answer: The bear narrative now sizes the rights-issue branch: one new share for four at a fifth off the market with the controller taking its full entitlement, so the share count rises a quarter and per-share value falls by more than earnings alone.

challenges.challenge: The Q3-2026 exit rate is used only as a downward check. Pack EBITDA of 645.5 plus the file's own D&A restatement of 71 gives 716.5 for the quarter, 2,866 annualised, 22% above FY2026E of 2,353.4 - and revenue rose for three consecutive quarters (1,257, 1,667, 2,075). The file cites only the lower of the two available run-rate methods (about 2,128).
challenges.answer: Re-answered on the post-reset model: FY2026E EBITDA 2,038.7, revenue 7,049.5 and D&A 303.0, with the four-quarter build about four per cent above and the exit-rate build about two-fifths above; section 3 states why the base sits below both. [S0]

challenges.challenge: Section 1 calls the parent offtake, an asset injection and a further tender the main source of upside optionality, and Section 5 says a float placement would migrate value toward Rp7,561, yet the bull is only a price and volume shock and the 20% liquidity discount applies in every scenario including the bull.
challenges.answer: The bull narrative now states plainly that it is a price, volume and unit-cost branch only, excluding the float remedy, any narrowing of the liquidity discount and any asset injection, all of which would add value outside it.

challenges.challenge: The summary says the El Nino event cuts both ways, but only the cost side is applied - FY2027 volume growth is removed while the deck price peak of 1,240 is untouched and the price benefit is admitted only in the bull. The same paragraph describes Rp3,940 as roughly half what the controller paid five months earlier, when the tender settled 3 March 2026 and control changed 19 November 2025.
challenges.answer: The summary now states the reviewed deck already carries the El Nino shortfall in its FY2027 peak above spot, so no separate price offset is added, and the elapsed time is corrected to the March 2026 tender, three months after the November 2025 control change.

challenges.challenge: Capex drops from the Rp600bn floor of the 600-800bn guidance to Rp565.6bn in FY2027 with no source, below the guided range, which raises FCFF in the years the DCF values most. Separately the volume basis says 350kt is not the floor of a guidance band, but S9 states average production between 350,000 and 400,000 tonnes.
challenges.answer: The FY2027 capex step-down is withdrawn: capex_unit holds the Rp600bn floor of the guided 600-800bn range in every year then escalates 3%, and the volume basis now says 350kt is the low end of the company band with the nine-month run-rate supporting it.

missing_bull_case.note: The bull (Rp11,198) is only a mirrored re-run of d.agri.cpo x1.2 and a.volume x1.05. Two quantified upside items are absent. First, the Q3-2026 exit rate: pack EBITDA 645.5 plus the file's own D&A restatement of 71 gives 716.5 a quarter, 2,866 annualised, 22% above FY2026E 2,353.4 - the higher of the two run-rate methods available and never shown. Second, the Section 1 offtake and injection routes carry zero value and zero probability in the bull.

missing_bear_case.note: Section 3 says a persistent higher unit cost would cut FY2026E EBITDA by roughly a quarter (about Rp590bn), yet the bear shocks only d.agri.cpo x0.8 and a.volume x0.95 (assumptions lines 333-347). The file's largest identified downside therefore carries no probability mass, and the bear narrative of a discounted rights issue or block placement has no numeric dilution either.

assumption_realism.note: The two biggest drivers are both unsourced and nearly offset. Realisation 1.00 against the 1.11 the audited FY2025 implies is worth about -Rp630bn of EBITDA; holding unit cash cost at the FY2025 Rp9.62m/t against the higher cost per tonne the four reported 2026 quarters print is worth about +Rp590bn. Net of both the evidence points about 8% above the base, but the file presents one as prudence and the other as its top risk.

evidence_and_citations.note: Thirteen of twenty-one sources are news or secondary, and the load-bearing estate facts (81,733 ha, eight mills, 350-400kt, 248,022t CPO) rest on one January 2026 Kontan piece S9. The D&A restatement of Rp303bn against a pack line of Rp19.1bn is a modelled assumption justified only by an unreachable website, and no source states the nature of the Rp808.89bn other operating expense whose Rp629.41bn excess is excluded.

valuation_method_fit.note: EV/EBITDA applies a clean 6.36x to the trailing 980.5 that the file itself normalises to 1,890.8; on its own normalised metric the cross-check is about Rp6,896, not Rp3,712, and the method blend moves to about Rp8,740. The own-history leg of that multiple (EV/EBITDA mean 7.13, n=4) is struck when the stock traded near Rp7,850 with a 34% float, the opposite regime to the 20% liquidity discount applied later. The bridge also pairs FY2025 EBITDA with 30 Sep 2026 net cash.

bias_and_tone.note: The prose says the El Nino event cuts both ways while only the volume cost is in the base, and calls the cross-check a floor while giving it 25% of the answer. Half the controller's price is described as five months earlier when the tender settled 3 March 2026 and control changed 19 November 2025, so eight to twelve months. Credit where due - the doubled-bear test in Section 5 replicates at about +37% total return.

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: Reads the right deck variables - d.agri.cpo in USD/t, costs in IDR, unit_factor 0.001, no royalty, export levy per tonne - and the peer convention difference (AALI nets the levy into a 0.78 realisation, SGRO charges it separately against gross revenue) is stated explicitly in Section 2. One gap - the levy is held flat at the November 2026 USD 246.36 while the ministry reference price of USD 978.90 sits 14% below the FY2026 deck price of 1,135, so the charge is not linked to the deck path.

conservatism_audit.note: Stacked. Realisation 1.00 vs 1.11 below the last actual (unsourced, about -Rp630bn EBITDA). Volume 350kt is the floor of the company's own 350,000-400,000t average band, and the basis text wrongly says it is not a band. Capex falls from the Rp600bn 2026 guidance floor to Rp565.6bn in FY2027 with no source, below the guided 600-800bn, which raises FCFF. Against that, D&A at 5% of gross PPE Rp6,164bn rather than net PPE Rp4,559bn overstates the tax shield. Price and volume shocks are properly mirrored at 0.8/1.2 and 0.95/1.05.

calibration.note: FY+1 at FY2025 prices and volume gives EBITDA 1,610 against 980.5 actual, and the qc justification for that 64% gap is internally inconsistent - it prices the realisation step-down at -Rp629bn and then says the model reproduces the last actual once that step-down is removed, while realisation is still 1.00. The model also compares FY2025A on the dirty pack basis (980.47, including the Rp629bn) with forecast years on the clean basis, so the +140% EBITDA jump is partly definitional.

signoff.notes: APPROVED conditional on four text/citation FIXes (Q1-Q4) and one NOTE (Q5) being applied to fund record before publication; none changes the BUY, the Rp5,555 target, the 50/25/25 weights or any engine number, and each is a wording or citation defect rather than a model one. Q1: the section 4 sentence must stop resting on the price/FX grid as printed. The grid 1.0/1.0 cell is Rp5,246 against a tp_base of Rp7,246, and it is the FX x1.1 row that reprints the base (Rp7,220); the CPO x0.8 cell at deck FX is Rp1,617, 59% below the Rp3,920 price, not close to it, and read transposed CPO x1.2 gives Rp7,220, below the Rp7,903 tender. The same offset appears in LSIP (centre 4,253 vs base 4,618), ANJT (2,933 vs 3,560) and CBUT (626 vs 732), so this is an engine artefact the analyst cannot fix in the model; the fix is to drop table:sensitivity or relabel it as an engine shock grid with the offset disclosed, and to state the downside and upside from the scenario values the target is built on: bear Rp1,751 (55% below the Rp3,920 price), base Rp7,246, bull Rp11,533. The volume/cost grid is centred correctly (1.0/1.0 = Rp7,246) and can carry the cost-sensitivity point. Q2: the 2028-03 catalyst and the first float paragraph of section 5 both attribute the staged one-eighth/15% to POJK 9/2018; S10 quotes POJK at 20% of paid-up within two years and S21 is the source for 12.5% by 31 March 2027 and 15% by 31 March 2028. Cite S21 for the stages and S10 for the 20% and the March 2028 deadline in both places; the thesis bullet already does this correctly. Q3: the rupiah move (FY2023A 15,229 to FY2026E 17,570) is the macro deck, not S16; S16 carries JISDOR 18,140 on 4 November and 18,183 on 28 October and neither cited number. Cite the macro deck, or quote the S16 figures. Q4: state the D&A base actually used - about 5% of average PPE of Rp6,164bn (the mean of the pack 7,769.1bn and 4,559.5bn), giving about Rp303bn, not 5% of gross 4,559.5bn, which is Rp228bn - and flag the Rp3,210bn FY2025 PPE fall against Rp387.1bn of capex as an unreconciled pack break before the D&A restatement is relied on. Q5: the printed COE build sums to 12.05%; the engine beta-scales the mature and country premia together, 5.83% + 0.89 x 6.69% = 11.78%, so reword to a beta-scaled equity risk premium of 6.7%. Keep the edit inside the 3,500-word update range (currently 3,497); Q6-Q8 are noted and do not block. REVIEW BASIS: engine ok (BUY, target Rp5,555, 53.5%), model_fresh, facts and lint PASS, engine_qc_blocking empty; calibration.ebitda (+36.0%) and extreme_call (+54%) are justified on the filing and the deck, and both justifications describe the model as built (half-charge inside opex, other_nonop zero, D&A restated). The base is the modal path rather than the cautious one: volume 353.5kt sits above the 9M CPO run-rate (248,022t annualises to 330.7kt) and on the company stated 350kt average; realisation 1.00 is calibrated on four-quarter FY2026 pack revenue (7,073.7bn run-rate against model 7,049.5bn), not the unmatched 1.11 FY2025 build; the FY2027 flat year is sourced to the GAPKI 2027-trough projection (S20); capex sits inside the Rp600-800bn guidance at its floor with FY2025 actual of Rp387.1bn below it; terminal growth at 3.0% is above the 2.5% most plantation peers use. The one unsourced conservatism is the Rp314.7bn recurring half-charge in opex, accepted in the prior round as the symmetric answer to an unexplained line and mirrored by the bear 1.15x unit-cost shock; the QC too_bearish note is recorded (effect inside 10% of target, BUY unchanged) and is not a publication blocker. Scenarios are mirrored (CPO 0.8/1.2, volume 0.95/1.05, cost 1.15/0.87), base 50%, and the Rp5,555 target reproduces exactly from the 6,944 weighted value times the 0.8 liquidity discount. Batch bias: SGRO is the only name in this packet; industry comps are mixed (CBUT, NSSS, PGUN, FAPA, JARR SELL), WACC 11.23% is inside the 11.18-11.42% peer range and g is above the peer mode, so no shared-input tilt. Not konglo; no consensus or broker material met.

bias.note:
Every departure from the last actual and the company plan points the same way. The Rp314.7bn
recurrent half of the FY2025 abnormal other operating expense is charged inside opex though no
source states its composition or that it recurs - S8 reports only that the line jumped from
Rp179.48bn to Rp808.89bn. Volume sits at the floor of management own 350,000-400,000t band [S9];
FY2027 is held flat against the company 3-5% ambition [S9, S11]; capex is pinned to the Rp600bn
floor of the Rp600-800bn guidance [S11]; and the 25%-weighted EV/EBITDA leg is struck on trailing
EBITDA of Rp980.5bn, which carries both the one-off and the pack partial D&A, against Rp1,261bn on
the model own restated D&A. Nothing in the stack points up, and FY2026E revenue of Rp7,049.5bn is
only 0.3% below the four-quarter pack run-rate, so the base is not optimistic. The direction is
too_bearish, though the total effect is well inside 10% of the target and does not change the BUY.

recomputed.item: FY2026 revenue run-rate (9M 4,998.6 + Q4 at Q3 2,075.1)

findings.finding:
Section 4 sensitivity sentence contradicts the engine grid it sits above. The grid no-shock
cell prints Rp5,246 (price/FX) and Rp6,713 (cost/volume) against a base target of Rp7,246, so a
1.0 multiplier is not the base case. As built, rows are IDR/USD and columns CPO: at deck FX,
CPO x0.8 gives Rp1,617, 59% below the Rp3,920 price, not close to it; read transposed, CPO
x1.2 gives Rp7,220, below the Rp7,903 tender, not well above. Either reading makes one clause
false, and the claim that the rupiah matters less than the commodity only holds on the correct
orientation.
findings.answer: Dropped the price/FX shock table and wrote the value range from the bear, base and bull scenario values instead; the cost point now rests on the correctly centred cost/volume grid, and the off-centre 1.0/1.0 cell can no longer be read as the base case.

findings.finding:
The front-matter catalyst dated 2028-03 states POJK 9/2018 deadline: public float restored to
the staged fifteen per cent minimum [S10]. S10 quotes the POJK requirement as at least 20% of
paid-up capital within two years of the tender completion, and F24 carries the same; 15% (and
12.5% first) is the BEI staged minimum from S21, not the POJK obligation. The report never
states the 20% figure anywhere, so it understates the shares that must come to market.
findings.answer: The 2028-03 catalyst and the section 5 governance paragraph now state the POJK 9/2018 endpoint as 20% of paid-up capital within two years [S10, F24], with the 12.5% by March 2027 and 15% by March 2028 staged path cited separately to S21.

findings.finding:
Section 2 says the rupiah has moved from 15,229 to 17,570 [S16]. S16 reports JISDOR at Rp18,140
on 4 November 2026 and Rp18,183 on 28 October and contains neither of the cited numbers; the
values are the macro deck FY2023A and FY2026E. The FY2026E 17,570 therefore sits 3.3% below the
spot the same article reports, and that gap is not reconciled.
findings.answer: The FX sentence now cites the deck/S0 for the FY2023 to FY2026 path and a new fact F39 for the 4 November JISDOR print of 18,140 [S16], so the forecast is explicitly compared with the weaker spot rather than cited to an article that does not carry it.

findings.finding:
Section 3 says D&A is restated to about five per cent of gross PPE of Rp4,559.5bn, which is
Rp228bn, but the model carries Rp303.0bn, which is 5% of average PPE of Rp6,164bn. The average
rests on a pack PPE series that falls from Rp7,769.1bn at FY2024 to Rp4,559.5bn at FY2025
against only Rp387.1bn of capex, and that Rp3,210bn break is nowhere explained or flagged.
findings.answer: D&A is now stated as about five per cent of average PPE with the opening FY2024 and closing FY2025 PPE printed, and the FY2025 PPE fall against capex is flagged as an unreconciled pack break controlled by the audited statement [S8].

findings.finding:
The section 4 cost-of-capital build as written ((7.45%-1.62%) + 0.89x4.23% + 2.46%) sums to
12.05%, not the printed 11.78%. The engine beta-scales the mature-market premium and the country
premium together (fund record line 572), so the printed figure is right and the sentence is
wrong.
findings.answer: The COE sentence now prints the build as the stripped rupiah yield plus levered beta times the sum of the mature-market and country premia, which reproduces the printed equity cost; no valuation input changed.

findings.finding:
Model net cash for FY2026E is Rp100.7bn while the valuation bridge uses the 30-Sep-2026 actual
net cash of Rp515.2bn; the Rp414.5bn implied fourth-quarter movement is disclosed in section 3
but not bridged, and ROE and interest income inherit the lower cash. Same as the judge first
note and prior round V7.

S4 says the acquisition adds 128,000 hectares of already-producing Papua estates to POSCO
portfolio (three mills, 210,000t/yr CPO capacity) while S9 puts SGRO at 81,733 hectares in
Sumatra and Kalimantan. Section 1 flags the non-reconciliation and models neither, which is
right, but if those hectares sit inside the listed company the 350kt volume base is materially
understated.

The report is at 3,497 words against the 500-3,500 update range (lint PASS, so the judge verdict
that it substantially exceeds the range is not right on the house range), and the FY2025
abnormal-expense explanation still recurs in the summary, sections 3, 5, 6 and 7.

flags.message: FY+1 priced at FY2025A benchmark and volume gives EBITDA 1,333.4 vs the actual 980.5 (+36%): reconcile costs, royalty or realisation with the filing, or justify the change
flags.justification: Reported FY2025 EBITDA is Rp980.5bn (EBIT 961.36 + pack D&A 19.1) [S0]. Repriced at the FY2025 benchmark of USD 1,007/t and 350kt, with the same cost structure, FY+1 gives Rp1,333.4bn (+36%), and every step is sourced. The whole Rp629.41bn excess of the FY2025 other operating expense over the prior year's Rp179.48bn comes out of opex (+629.4) [S8]; D&A is restated from the pack's partial line to the modelled Rp303bn (+284) [S0]; half the excess, Rp314.7bn, is charged forward inside opex (-314.7), so the recurring half now reaches EBIT and FCFF rather than sitting below EBIT [S8]. The repricing converts the dollar price at the FY2026 deck rupiah of 17,570 rather than FY2025's 16,448, a gain, while realisation is 1.00 against the 1.11 the FY2025 audited revenue implies [S8, S9], removing the kernel and seed mix the 2026 data do not reproduce, and the per-tonne export charge is repriced; those three net to about -245. Sum: 980.5 + 629.4 + 284.0 - 314.7 - 245 = 1,333. No unsourced step remains: volume is the company's 350kt average, cost is the FY2025 reconciliation and the charge is the one the file carries in the base [S0, S8, S9, S11].

flags.message: expected return +54%: name the two or three sourced drivers that produce it and what today's price implies (reverse DCF)
